A Message from Iran to the American People and Everyone Who Stands for Peace, Freedom, and the Oppressed

Hello, I am writing to you from Iran. I hope that my message will reach the people of the United States and everyone around the world who believes in peace and freedom and stands in solidarity with the oppressed.

Why People Should Be Concerned About Endless Wars

One of the most dangerous habits of great powers in our time is turning war into something normal. Attacking countries, sanctioning nations, issuing constant threats, stationing troops across the world, and spending billions and trillions of dollars of public money are sometimes repeated so casually in the official language of governments that it seems as if it is a natural and even necessary thing. But there is nothing natural about destruction, insecurity, bloodshed, and the waste of public wealth. No informed nation should accept that its life, welfare, and future be sacrificed for military ambitions and power games.

People of every country, including the American people, have the right to ask themselves why the product of their labor and taxes should be spent on wars that bring neither real security nor lasting peace. When billions of dollars are spent on missiles, bombs, military bases, and foreign interventions, that same money is no longer available for better schools, cheaper healthcare, safer infrastructure, affordable housing, and a secure future for the younger generation. War does not only destroy the other side of the borders; it also leaves behind poverty, exhaustion, debt, and moral crisis inside the warmongering country itself.

For years, people have been told that these wars are for the defense of freedom, security, and peace. But experience has shown time and again that many of these interventions have not brought peace, but have instead created hatred, displacement, instability, and deeper wounds. The nations whose countries are targeted by attacks or sanctions pay a heavy human cost: children are deprived of education and safety, families are displaced, economies collapse, and generations grow up with fear and despair. No political narrative can hide the simple truth that human lives should not be tools for maintaining influence or geopolitical interests.

On the other hand, normalizing permanent enemy-making for the public allows governments to justify huge military budgets every time under a new pretext. The more the fear, the less the questioning. The bigger the enemy is portrayed, the easier the military waste is accepted. In such an atmosphere, citizens, instead of being monitors of power, become consumers of official narratives. This is where public awareness becomes important. People must ask themselves who benefits from war and who pays the price. Usually, the profits go into the pockets of military-industrial complexes, military contractors, and power networks, while the cost is paid by ordinary families, soldiers, taxpayers, and defenseless nations.

No country becomes more moral, secure, or humane by constantly bombing others. Real security is achieved through justice, mutual respect, diplomacy, economic cooperation, and avoiding domination, not through spreading fear and destruction. People who want a better future for their children must demand their leaders to spend national wealth on healing the real pains of society instead of wasting it in far-off wars. A hospital that is built is more valuable than a missile that is fired. A school that is developed is more honorable than a base established on the soil of others. Peace, although less profitable for warmongers, builds a more humane future for nations.
